text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC — thinking out loud about FP8/INT8/INT4 attention + where dequant fusion should live. TL;DR: propose runtime-level policy + lightweight kernel hinting, not forcing fusion into every kernel. Thoughts?

alex: +1 to runtime policy. If we bake fusion into every kernel variant we explode QA surface. prefer a small, well-tested fused path and generic kernels for everything else.

sam: can you outline the perf tradeoffs? fusion wins on latency right? by how much?

maria: Good Q. Microbenchmarks (L=1..2048) show fused dequant+attn gives ~20-40% lower p50 for short sequences versus separate dequant + attn for INT8/FP8 on A100. For long sequences fusion sometimes loses due to memory-copy patterns.

priya: We should also consider numeric stability for FP8. Fusing changes reduction order and can mask calibration errors. Need instrumentation to surface per-token outliers.

jin: On KV cache implications: fused kernels need to preserve same KV layout contract. If fusion shuffles layout (e.g., interleaved dequantization into KV), rolling back will be painful. I'd push for strict memory-contract tests.

alex: about kernel registry API, propose adding an optional "hints" field so runtime can ask for a fused path when available. Example: 
```
register_kernel({
  op: "attention",
  dtype: "int8",
  hints: ["dequant_fused", "kv_contiguous"],
  cost_model: "perf.json"
})
```
Then runtime picks kernels that match policy.

maria: I like that. keeps kernels small and composable. Also runtime can fall back to (dequant -> attn) chain if fused kernel fails. Need fast health-check path.

sam: fallback latency penalty is my worry. If fused path is unhealthy we must auto-circuit to next best with minimal disruption. Can we pre-warm fallback kernels in same process?

maria: yes — prewarm + keepwarm tokens. runtime can maintain a hot-slot per-device for N kernel variants. If fused fails, switch pointer and keep the KV/caches pinned.

priya: Also add a calibration tag on kernel metadata: e.g., `requires_calibration: true` and `calib_version: "v2"`. That way model deploys with mismatched calibration get a hard warning.

jin: Memory alignment: INT4/INT8 packed formats need 32B alignment for our optimized attention. Fused kernels often assume packed layout. Runtime should provide an allocator that can return compatible buffers and a fast path to repack small batches.

alex: What about quant-range metadata per model? Do we store min/max or some per-head scale? I prefer storing per-layer scale factors in model meta so kernels don't guess.

maria: agreed. store per-layer scales in model manifest and expose them to runtime at load time. If missing, runtime falls back to on-the-fly calibration (slower) and flags the model.

sam: Risk: on-the-fly calib is non-deterministic across replicas. Need deterministic seed/steps and a check-sum of calib outputs to avoid silent divergence.

priya: +1. Also log calibration histograms to the Console (opt-in) for regression detection.

alex: ops note — deploy-bot: we should have a canary plan. Start with 10% traffic to fused kernels on Dedicated pools only, with auto-rollback on error rate or latency spike.

maria: +1. Canary criteria: ERR > 0.5% OR p95 > baseline*1.3 OR token-drop events. If triggered, rollback and attach trace.

jin: Side note: for INT4 we should avoid hyper-aggressive fusion initially. INT4 packing amplifies tiny calibration errors; prefer FP8 and INT8 first.

priya: FP8 path is promising but needs exponent bias handling clearly specified in kernel contract. Let's add `fp8_variant` tag (e4m3/e5m2) to kernel metadata.

alex: Example kernel metadata shape (proposal): 
```
metadata: {
  tags: ["dequant_fused","kv_contiguous"],
  requires_calibration: "true",
  calib_hash: "sha256:...",
  fp8_variant: "e4m3",
  mem_layout: "packed32b",
  perf_bucket: "short_seq_opt"
}
```
This stays flat and easy to index.

maria: Good. Implementation plan: 1) Add hints/tags field to kernel registry (PR next week). 2) Runtime: implement policy selector + hot-slot prewarm (prototype). 3) Create one fused INT8 attention kernel with strict KV contract + canary. 4) Add model manifest scale metadata and calib checksum.

sam: Who owns the fused kernel? eng-runtime or eng-ml? My vote: eng-ml implements prototype, eng-runtime integrates into registry and rollout.

maria: Agreed. eng-ml to own numeric correctness and calibration infra, eng-runtime owns registry/selection/rollout.

jin: Testing matrix: device types (A100/H100), seq lengths [1,64,512,2048], batch sizes [1,8,32], dtypes [fp8,int8,int4], kv-layout variants. We'll need hardware time.

priya: I'll schedule some benchmarks on H100 and share scripts. Also add eval prompts to check generation drift with fused vs baseline.

alex: Implementation gotcha: kernel compiled with different compilers or flags may produce slightly different FP8 scaling. enforce `compiler_id` tag in metadata.

maria: Nice catch. Add `build_id`/`compiler_id` to kernel metadata and require matching on selection unless policy allows cross-build mixing.

sam: Ops & observability: surface a metric for "dequant_fused_used_ratio" per model route + per-device. That helps adoption and regression detection.

maria: Done. We'll add that to Console and to the rollout dashboard.

build-bot: CI: fused-int8-attn prototype build completed on h100-lab-3, perf numbers uploaded to /artifacts/fused_int8_v1/bench.csv : 25-38% lower p50 on short seq.

maria: Thanks @build-bot. Next steps: I'll spin up an RFC follow-up doc with the proposed metadata fields and rollout plan, then sync with eng-ml tomorrow. If nobody objects, I'll open the registry-change PR by EOD Thursday.

taylor: No objections from me. One ask: include an escape hatch to opt a route out of fused kernels entirely (config flag) in case customers need deterministic numeric parity.

maria: Yep — route-level `disable_fused_kernels: true` is on the plan.

alex: Great thread. I'll draft the registry PR and ping y'all for review. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks everyone — feel free to drop quick comments here if you see any missing risks.

priya: Adding a note — we should think about telemetry privacy: if calibration histograms include sample tokens we must scrub or aggregate.

maria: Good call, Priya. We'll send only aggregated stats by default and make raw samples opt-in for debugging.

jin: That addresses my KV layout and alignment concerns. excited to see the prototype.

sam: I'll prepare the fallback prewarm plan (short doc) and link it to the RFC.

maria: Awesome — closing this thread for now, will post the RFC link once it's up."
